instruction_problem: Present (am standing/turns) and past (was standing/turned) both work; 'hands' is present so past is less consistent but a learner may well write it. Task does not force the anecdote present.
level_problem: Anecdote present is C1 use, but 'stand' for the first gap pair needs two words; fine.

answer: I was waiting for the bus when suddenly this car stops right in front of me.
wrong_options_that_fit: Option 4 ('this man is walking into a café and he orders') is borderline: joke/anecdote narration is normally 'walks', 'is walking ... and orders' is odd but possible; it could fit as a mistake too.
sense_problem: Option 1 mixes past continuous with present 'stops' - a plausible learner error. Option 4 is also unnatural, so two options are arguably wrong.

instruction_problem: Past forms are wrong for live commentary only if the learner knows the context; 'passes ... shoots and scores' is the intended one; 'passed ... shot' would not fit 'scores'. Task is fine.
level_problem: Commentary present is nearer B1/B2 than C1; a B1 learner could solve it.
